intent: Show that between 1990 and 2017, Sub-Saharan Africa's illiteracy rate fell more slowly, in proportional terms, than in Latin America & Caribbean, East Asia & Pacific, and the European Union.

requirements.question: How did the illiteracy rate change from 1990 to 2017 in the four regions?
Which region improved least in relative terms?

units.claim: From 1990 to 2017 the illiteracy rate fell in all four regions: Sub-Saharan Africa 48%→36.1%, Latin America & Caribbean 15.5%→6.9%, East Asia & Pacific 18%→5.1%, European Union 2%→1%.
accept: all four absolute declines (11.9, 8.6, 12.9, 1 percentage points)
units.evidence: Four endpoint pairs or four declines are visible.

units.claim: Sub-Saharan Africa's proportional decline is the smallest (about 25%), below Latin America & Caribbean (55%), the European Union (50%) and East Asia & Pacific (72%), so its illiteracy rate improved more slowly.
accept: relative-decline ranking: East Asia & Pacific > Latin America & Caribbean > European Union > Sub-Saharan Africa
Sub-Saharan Africa improved least in proportional terms
reject: Sub-Saharan Africa declined the least in percentage points (the EU's absolute drop is the smallest)
units.evidence: Four relative declines, or a visual that shows Sub-Saharan Africa improved proportionally least.
